title: The distinction between sounds and spiritual words
english: Those grasping life treasure in heaven, having their heart there; the heavens are narrating the previously spoken glory of God through the contemplation of intelligible things. But those who have accepted the practical [aspect] accomplish a firmament through works, that is, they become stable and immovable; they announce the making of the hands of God, working the works of God and through them crying out as works becoming the works of God.

But also the day, that is, the luminous intellect, being not in harmony with another luminous intellect, searches out a word, which is why the Old Scripture says the day is luminous: for God called the light Day (Gen 1:5). This, having been filled with the nourishments of the Spirit, being searched out from the fullness, a word is brought forth in the New Covenant; allegorically also this day is so named.

And the night, the deepest discourse of things, announces knowledge to another such night. For if anyone searches the Spirit who searches all things and has the depths of God, he searches some of the deeper mysteries of God; having known it from this, he proceeds to the similarly obscure, and will come to the knowledge of those.

And the pre-preparations and those making the way forward are mere babblings, but the words were those setting forth the spiritual narratives and fully bringing their faiths demonstratively. The sounds and words for the obedience of God are not, since their voices are not heard as Being. For this reason it has been said by the Lord, so that they might be heard (Matt 25:4): therefore no word of apology is left to those not doing nor thinking; the voices of the previously spoken babblings and words are being narrated. Their sound has gone out into all the earth (Ps 19:4), and the following.

You are a land suitable for seed (Matt 13:23), but you do not receive the sound of the babblings and words, that is, the word according to the sensible [aspect] of the Scripture; but those having surpassed the state of these will receive the words of the babblings and the words, being clearly instructed in all things. Even the precursor of the apostles is not hearing the sound of Jesus but words; 'Words,' he says, 'you have of eternal life'; and the Savior himself: 'The words I have spoken to you are spirit' (John 6:63). For those which he said to the apostles, no longer...

title: The Hidden Sins and Divine Cleansing
english: The Lord's testimony, which testifies through good works and the knowledge of truth, is faithful. It is called faithful not from the act of believing, but from the worthiness of being believed, just as the Word 'Faithful' is said of the Faithful One, and concerning God it is said, 'God is faithful and there is no injustice in him' (1 Cor 10:13) and 'God is faithful through whom you were called' (1 Cor 1:9). For because of worthiness and the being worthy of being believed, it was so named, but also because of the certain and unchangeable nature. Thus indeed the Lord's faithful testimony makes wise those who have turned and become like children according to the will of Jesus.

And it makes wise even the newborn infants, those born through the gospel. Perhaps it also makes wise those little ones who have not been trained by disciplines and with the exercises of human words, but the unlettered and the laypeople. And the commands of the Lord, being outside of all crookedness, are straight, making straight those who receive them, so that they might cast off all sorrow and become in divine joy the soul.

And the fear of God is said to be pure, not a passion that casts one out from perfect love, but the same one that is characterized by piety and divine reverence. It does not work out the state of those who are merely fittingly pure, but it extends even unto the age to come, not being transient and short-lived. The judgments of the Lord are true. He who performs all things according to His own truth and judges, judges truly; as the apostle says: 'For the judgment of God is according to truth upon those practicing such things' (Rom 2:2). God judges according to truth, and the judgments are true—it is said 'true' in contrast to false and unjust judgments.

These true judgments are justified in the same way, whatever may happen, and in the same way it may become. For perhaps if anyone wished to see its truth and justice by itself, he would not clearly see it; for they testify to one another as whatever is, is to be held as testifying. These things, having been foreseen by the one who applied his own mind, are desirable, more precious than those among men. For he who has turned away his own desiring power from gold and precious stones, with longing toward the...

He will consume all of it into truly desirable things, and he will perceive the sweetness of these things more sweetly than the sweetness of a garden and honey in the senses. He will not taste it bodily, but by a divine sense he will perceive the sweetness of the things mentioned before. The servant of the Lord keeps these things. For indeed your servant keeps them; he is not saying this about himself alone, but also about every servant of the Lord. If one turns toward the guarding of these things something temporary and sensible, the recompense is not great; but since the recompense for the guarding of these things is supra-cosmic and supra-heavenly, it follows that it is great.

Everyone is aware of the manifest and effective sins, but the transgressions occurring in secret in the thoughts and reasonings, the one who sees them is rare; for who declares what is rare here? Paul, therefore, not being aware of anything to himself, knowing what is the rare thing to understand the aforementioned transgressions, says, 'Not in this [I am justified]' (cf. Rom 3:28). Furthermore, regarding the transgressions, who will understand? It lies [to say], 'From my secret things cleanse me' (Ps 18:14c). This is said only by the righteous, since defilement occurs in the secret reasonings of the heart, which not only others but I myself am ignorant of; you, remove it, being a knower of those things which happen in secret. For this defilement, if it is not destroyed, becomes an increased starting-point and pretext to be captured by others; sparing your servant, do not let him be captured by others, having cleansed him from the secret things. For the sins occurring in secret, if not being cut off, may at some time pass over into practical sin, through which one might be involved with the things of God or with evil powers. God will spare his own servant, but if he does not spare his own Son, having handed him over above all, it is the loss of the Son for all, and not sparing leads to being [lost] for the salvation of all. And the Son himself will be outside of all harm, not receiving this even by nature.

He says [it is] a great sin, the effective one (Ps 18:15). For if he is not cleansed from my secret things, these transgressions remaining carry over into bad practice, and I become responsible for a great sin. If these...

title: The Beauty of the Savior and the Fulfillment of Prayer
english: If [the words] exist from you, then the words of my mouth are for acceptance; for I have previously prayed to you, praising you and thanking you; and the words of acceptance are worthy. The study of my intellect, occurring in thoughts and notions, is found always before you, free from all reproach. However, the praiseworthy study is not from another but has risen from you, having cleansed me from my secret faults. With you helping, O Lord, I fall not to any who fight against me spiritually. But if, through my inattention, I should be seized by the adversaries, you redeem me from those who have seized me, as you are found to be my helper and redeemer.

The one who is afflicted, making him joyful, is the word that exists in the soul, or the Holy Spirit who awakens him, he says (Ps 19:2–4): 'The Lord will hear you in a day of affliction.' Through progress, the afflicted learns not to be meager nor to cast down hopes, but to pour out [himself] to God through prayers; for prayer leads to hearing God. He does not urge the afflicted to pray in order to appear [pious]; 'The Lord will hear you in a day of affliction, and the name of the God of Jacob will protect you' (Ps 91:15). The presence of God, which has been made to dwell in Jacob, being a shield, is from you. One should seek why, God having enriched Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the name of the God of Jacob, and not the God of Abraham and Isaac, protects the afflicted. Perhaps it is because, since Jacob has become in many sufferings and hardships as if his life were a symbol of the athletic life, the afflicted, practicing to endure tribulations and contending against them, is protected by the presence of God, which is that of Jacob, so that he, having become a wing-beater because of that, may flutter and strike down the afflictions and the evil spirits working them.

And from a holy [place] the help is sent, that of the heavenly temple (for the temple is called holy among the Hebrews), which is from the holy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, it is said concerning: 'God from the heights and the Holy One from the strong Pharaoh shall overshadow like a dense cloud' (Ps 89:10). But the explanation will be mastered from the approaching verse. 'For from Zion shall He take hold of you, from there...'

The splendor of the Savior's beauty shines upon the race of men according to 'Out of Zion'. The first reading is understood as 'Out of the heavenly Zion of God'. 'May all your sacrifice be remembered', he prays, signifying this for the one being afflicted: that he will be released from this affliction as if he had offered a sacrifice thankfully, so that God may remember all your sacrifice, which is not such a sacrifice as is being approached, but a spiritual one. 'But also accepting your burnt offering, let it ascend'; it should be noted that a burnt offering differs from a sacrifice. For perhaps the name of sacrifice is laid upon the soulless things brought to the altar, whereas a burnt offering is a living victim.

Ps 19:5: God gives according to the heart of the one praying, whatever such things he requests; and it is proper to give to God, and it is beneficial to the receiver. For the prayer concerning these things, being done rightly, satisfies God. And 'to fulfill all your counsel'; counsel, that is, to fulfill the counsel being done rightly. And a counsel is fulfilled if it does not fail in its intentions, but meets those things about which it was pre-counseled.

Ps 19:6: And this is what is said concerning it: 'Behold, a Savior was born to us, who is Christ the Lord.' It is said that to speak of salvation is to speak of the salvation which is being saved, to whom God hearkens in a day of affliction, in which salvation there will be rejoicing. And 'we shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God'. Unlike those being magnified in worldly things, we 'shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God'. 'We shall be magnified' signifies progress in such goodness. For it does not say: 'We are great'. In this way, Isaac, as he went forward, became greater, as he became very great. And someone is magnified in the name of the Lord by performing the work of a genuine and perfect servant. A great encomium regarding that about which the word is: 'all his requests shall be fulfilled by the Lord, asking nothing which God does not provide'. And the fulfillment of requests is to emerge and come into abundance regarding those things for which someone was worthy.
